rules.name: Owner_Is_User_On_Update
rules.label: Owner Is User (newly set on update)

Flow.description:
Stamps AF_AssignedDateTime__c when OwnerId becomes a User (on create, or on an update that actually changes the owner — not on every edit), then calls AF_BusinessHoursService to compute the three SLA targets against the Lead's business-unit Business Hours record, so targets genuinely respect Friday-off / working-hours boundaries instead of plain calendar time.
Runs after-save (before-save flows cannot call Apex actions), and writes back with one Update Records call keyed to $Record — this does not re-enter the flow's own entry criteria, since the resulting DML is an Update to fields other than OwnerId.
FIXED 2026-08-16: Added entry criteria filterFormula NOT({!$Record.IsConverted}) to prevent flow from running during lead conversion, which was causing "Unable to convert lead that is in use by workflow" error due to record locks during the conversion transaction.
CHANGED 2026-08-26 (business decision, BRD 8.6 open item "SLA clock start point: lead creation vs. queue assignment" — resolved by Yassin in favour of ASSIGNMENT): all rules require OwnerId to be a User (005 prefix). The SLA clock no longer starts while a Lead sits unassigned in a BU queue — it starts the moment a Manager/Supervisor assigns it to a real agent. This reverses the 2026-08-16 "fire on ANY create regardless of owner type" workaround, which was only ever needed because AF_FL_Lead_RoundRobinAssignment auto-assigned every Lead to a person at creation, so nothing ever genuinely sat in a queue. With round-robin retired (LFRDN-606) and AF_FL_Lead_QueueRouting now placing new Leads in the correct BU queue, queued Leads are the normal state and must NOT have a running SLA clock.
FIXED 2026-08-27: the 2026-08-26 change had a race condition. Lead Assignment Rules (AF_AR_Lead_Routing) run AFTER after-save flows in Salesforce's save order — so on Lead creation, this flow's create-path branch always saw the record's temporary pre-routing owner (the creating user, a 005 Id) BEFORE AF_AR_Lead_Routing had a chance to reassign OwnerId to a BU Queue later in the same transaction. Result: SLA silently started for every new Lead regardless of whether it ended up Queue-owned, contradicting the 2026-08-26 decision — confirmed identically in both DEV and QA (a platform execution-order issue, not an environment misconfiguration). Fixed by removing the synchronous create-path branch entirely and moving the "owner is a User but SLA still blank" backfill onto a Run-Asynchronously scheduled path (0 hours after CreatedDate, timeSource RecordField — RecordTriggerEvent time source is rejected by the platform on a Create/CreateAndUpdate-triggered flow, "Configure the flow to run only when a record is updated"). Scheduled paths execute after the triggering transaction — including Assignment Rules — fully commits, so by the time this path evaluates OwnerId, routing has already resolved and the true final owner is visible. The synchronous "Owner Is User (newly set on update)" branch is kept for the common manual-reassignment case (Queue → Agent) so SLA appears immediately without waiting on the async path.
FIXED 2026-08-27 (same day, follow-up): the new async scheduled path introduced a SECOND source of the exact RECORD_IN_USE_BY_WORKFLOW error already fought in AF_LeadConversionService.clearPendingSlaScheduledActions() (which bounces OwnerId to a Queue and back to cancel AF_FL_Lead_SLAEscalation's pending scheduled paths — that trick works because AF_FL_Lead_SLAEscalation's entry criteria depends on AF_IsOwnerAUser__c, so the OwnerId bounce makes it stop matching and Salesforce auto-cancels the pending action). This flow's filterFormula was only NOT({!$Record.IsConverted}) — it does not reference OwnerId at all, so the same queue-bounce trick did NOT cancel this flow's newly-added scheduled action, meaning any Lead with a still-pending async backfill action would hit the same conversion-blocking error again. Fixed by adding {!$Record.AF_IsOwnerAUser__c} to the filterFormula so this flow (and therefore its scheduled path registration) only ever enters when OwnerId currently resolves to a real User — harmless to intended behavior (both the update branch and the async backfill branch already require OwnerId StartsWith "005" internally to do anything), and now correctly cancellable by the exact same existing mitigation.
FIXED 2026-08-28: Call_FinalDisposition_Target's durationMillis was 2.592E8 (72 hours = 3 x 24), assuming a 24-hour business day. The actual configured Business Hours (AF_BH_Automobiles/PremierMotors/SportsMotors) are only 08:00-20:00 (12 hours/day), 6 days/week (Friday off). BusinessHours.add() treats durationMillis as elapsed BUSINESS time, not calendar time, so 72 business-hours took 6 real working days to elapse (72 / 12), stretching a "3 day" SLA target out to roughly a full calendar week once the Friday closure was skipped over. The BRD (8.6 FR4) explicitly wants thresholds "calculated against the configured working calendar" (so business-hours-aware is correct), but the duration itself should represent 3 WORKING days, not 3 x 24 raw hours. Fixed to 1.296E8 (36 hours = 3 x 12, matching the actual configured business day length). Fragile: this hardcodes today's 12-hour business day; if any BU's Business Hours record is ever changed to a different daily length, this constant would need updating too — the other two targets (15 min, 1 hour) don't have this problem since they're far shorter than one business day.

formulas.name: AF_Formula_BusinessHoursName
formulas.expression: CASE({!$Record.AF_BusinessUnit__c}, "Alfardan Automobiles", "AF_BH_Automobiles", "Alfardan Premier Motors", "AF_BH_PremierMotors", "Alfardan Sports Motors", "AF_BH_SportsMotors", "AF_BH_Automobiles")
